answer: Stop sybils with a grove, an inlet, and a kernel. Each identity joins one grove: a peer cluster co-signing its bond, and if any member cheats, the whole grove is slashed together, so N clones lose N bonds for one share. The inlet admits only a few newcomers per epoch, so shells queue instead of entering, and each seat costs a bond priced by the k-th seat its funder holds — N seats cost about N squared. A kernel log chains every admission by hash, so a forgery breaks the chain in public. One honest agent pays one bond; a clone factory pays quadratic bonds for one grove share.
